title: Balanced equations and reacting masses; Molar gas volume and Avogadro's law
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AM07#t4 term and clue written for the game; AM07#t3 term and clue written for the game; AM07#t1 term and clue written for the game; AM07#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM05#N.2, AM07#N.4a, AM05#N.4, AM07#N.6a, AM05#N.7b, AM07#N.12a, AM05#N.10b, AM07#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Precipitate
items.clue: A solid formed when two solutions react, e.g. AgCl from Ag⁺ and Cl⁻.

items.label: State symbols
items.clue: The labels (s), (l), (g) and (aq) written after each species in an equation.

items.label: Coefficient
items.clue: A number that multiplies a whole formula and gives the ratio of amounts in moles.

items.label: Spectator ions
items.clue: Dissolved species that appear unchanged on both sides of an equation and are left out.

questions.stem: Two identical sealed flasks are at the same temperature and pressure. One is filled with methane, CH₄, and the other with chlorine, Cl₂. The methane flask contains 5.00 × 10²² atoms in total. How many atoms does the chlorine flask contain? (Ar: H 1.0, C 12.0, Cl 35.5)
questions.explanation: Equal molecules: 5.00 × 10²² ÷ 5 = 1.00 × 10²² CH₄ molecules, so 1.00 × 10²² Cl₂ molecules = 2.00 × 10²² atoms.

questions.stem: Aluminium burns in oxygen to form aluminium oxide. Which equation for this reaction is correctly balanced?
questions.explanation: Al₂O₃ and O₂ are the right formulae. 3O₂ gives 6 O = 2Al₂O₃, which needs 4Al. 4 Al and 6 O each side.

questions.stem: Sulfur dioxide reacts with oxygen: 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2SO₃(g). What volume of oxygen reacts completely with 30.0 cm³ of sulfur dioxide? All volumes are measured at the same temperature and pressure.
questions.explanation: Same T and p, so volumes are in the coefficient ratio: 30.0 × 1/2 = 15.0 cm³.

questions.stem: Magnesium ribbon fizzes and dissolves in dilute hydrochloric acid. Which is the ionic equation for the reaction?
questions.explanation: Cl⁻ is a spectator. 1 Mg and 2 H each side; charge 2+ each side.

questions.stem: Magnesium reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid: Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂(g). What volume of hydrogen, in cm³, forms from 0.120 g of magnesium at 20 °C and 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa? (Ar: Mg 24.3; R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)

Iron is produced by reducing iron(III) oxide with carbon monoxide: Fe₂O₃(s) + 3CO(g) → 2Fe(s) + 3CO₂(g). What is the maximum mass of iron that can be produced from 40.0 g of iron(III) oxide? (Ar: O 16.0, Fe 55.8)

Two identical 500 cm³ flasks are at 25 °C and 1.00 × 10⁵ Pa. One is filled with neon, Ne, and one with sulfur hexafluoride, SF₆, a dense gas used in electrical switchgear. The SF₆ flask holds 7.2 times the mass of gas. Which statement is correct? (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹; Ar: F 19.0, Ne 20.2, S 32.1)

options.text: Each flask holds 2.02 × 10⁻² mol of gas.
Each flask holds 2.41 × 10⁻¹ mol of gas.
Each flask holds 20.2 mol of gas.
The neon flask holds 2.02 × 10⁻² mol, the SF₆ flask 2.79 × 10⁻³ mol.

questions.explanation: n = pV/RT = (1.00 × 10⁵ × 5.00 × 10⁻⁴) ÷ (8.31 × 298) = 2.02 × 10⁻² mol. Nothing in pV = nRT depends on which gas it is.

questions.stem: A strip of magnesium burns brightly in air and leaves white magnesium oxide: 2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s). What mass of MgO forms from 2.43 g of Mg? (Ar: O 16.0, Mg 24.3)
